analysis.title: European Equity Daily (2nd November)
key_insights: UK Budget delivered tweaks rather than wholesale change and deferred tougher fiscal decisions. Macro impact looks limited, but Jefferies analysts see sector implications for Banks, Utilities, Gaming, Defence and Housebuilders.

Initiation: PPC at Buy. It offers the highest growth among Jefferies' Euro Utilities coverage at a sector-average valuation. SE Europe has attractive structural dynamics and PPC's balance sheet gives it capacity to invest.
Orion upgraded to Buy. The Nubeqa exclusivity extension and pipeline optionality are underappreciated, and a March '27 litigation could extend US exclusivity to 2036.
Danone upgraded to Hold after de-rating to ~15x P/E. Risk-reward is more balanced, but Jefferies stays cautious on US Dairy and China Nutrition fundamentals.
SCA downgraded to Hold after a 22% rally. Improved containerboard pricing is increasingly reflected in expectations, further upside needs a recovery in pulp and wood, and 2027 expectations run ahead.
GSK downgraded to Hold. Reduced earnings momentum, launch execution risk and fewer pipeline catalysts limit re-rating potential despite a valuation discount.

Veolia reinstated at Hold. Its low valuation reflects a low single digit growth outlook as boosters under-deliver, mix is shifting to lower-margin activities, and the FY27 EBITDA target requires acceleration.
Genmab retained at Buy (Franchise Pick) after solid Phase III headlines for peto this week, which de-risk the locally advanced setting.
Schneider Electric reiterated at Buy. A guidance upgrade, financing progress and software channel checks de-risk the PTC deal, and improved PTC performance supports timing and valuation.

Japan quant: the TOPIX restructuring puts 683 stocks at risk of removal by July 2028, with free-float improvements, crossholding unwinds or parent buyouts as potential upside catalysts ahead of the August 2027 review.

US Power & Utilities sell-off continues despite improving pipeline and power visibility. Multiples have compressed and risk appetite is low, but valuation dispersion is widening and catalysts are emerging.
India NSE initiated at Buy, with 15% revenue and 16% EPS CAGR through FY29. Its premium to BSE is viewed as justified.

Semis: hyperscaler 2026 capex expectations were broadly unchanged. 2027 outlooks from KLA, ASM, SK Hynix and TEL were constructive for semicap. Monolithic Power raised Enterprise data growth expectations to over 150%, positive for IFX, and reports of Marvell buying Lumentum lifted optical suppliers.

Rheinmetall Q3 (5 Nov): Jefferies expects 39% sales growth and 51% adj. EBIT growth. No guide change is expected, but the year-end backlog target could be questioned depending on the Arminius contract signing in Q4.
Leonardo Q3 (5 Nov): expects 14% sales growth and 29% EBITA growth, likely paving the way for a guide upgrade.

US banks: 26 of 34 banks beat 3Q EPS, often on lower provisions. Deposits (20 misses) and fees (18) lagged, credit stayed benign, and the late-quarter rate spike widened AOCI losses and slowed buybacks. 2027 EPS was raised for 19 banks, kept for 7 and cut for 8.

AI cloud: mega cloud backlog hit $2.5T (+106% y/y) and y/y cloud growth accelerated to 57% from 48%. MSFT Azure grew 48% CC, GOOGL and AMZN lagged, and rising capex drove a rotation into FCF software compounders. CY27 capex estimates (including SPCX) reach $1.5T.
Q3 US earnings: with 60% of the S&P 500 reported, earnings growth is tracking ~32% and sales ~13.5%. The rest of the index is expected to outgrow the Mag 7, 35% vs 23%.
October performance: Small ahead YTD, Value leads Growth, non-earners in the Russell fell 8.1% and highest beta fell 8.6%. 64.4% of managers beat in October, 47% YTD.
ETF flows: outflows from Large Core, Large Value and QQQ, about $1B of inflows to Small, and $1.4B into High Yield, which ended a three-week outflow streak.
Russell rebalance on December 11: the R2 top-end cutoff is $9.7B and SPCX faces ~$10.5B of buying pressure on increased float.
Macro: French government debt selling may be driven by Japanese holders. Jefferies' Mohit expects only one more ECB hike (Dec), ending the cycle.

Middle East remains the macro wildcard in energy, with post-midterm escalation risk threatening Gulf infrastructure and shipping, and diesel, jet fuel and freight exposed. Indian crude basket is at US$115/bbl.
Copper: 3Q26 aggregate production from miners representing ~65% of supply fell 3.1% y/y and 0.7% q/q, YTD down 3.0%, keeping price risk skewed to the upside if global growth holds.

Cameco Q3 EPS of C$0.01 missed Jefferies by C$0.35 and consensus by C$0.32. FY26 production guidance top end was lowered to 19.5-20.5Mlb. Industry long-term contracting is 33% below the replacement rate.
Boeing reaffirmed ~$2B 2026 FCF but delayed the ~$10B FCF target by a year to 2029. Jefferies cut BCA deliveries by 5% across 2026-2029, to 640 in 2026.

Aerospace and defense Q3 prints were strong: GD sales and profit 6% ahead with 2026 EPS raised to $17.35, ARXS raised 2026 guidance with 2027 sales and EBITDA framework 3%/6% ahead, TXT 2026 EPS raised 14% to $6.65, while HONA 2027 EPS was cut 4% to $8.65.
Software: IGV fell 6% last week and Jefferies stays defensive on the AI-cycle crosscurrents, favoring MSFT, IBM and ADSK, and DT for offense.
Software/Services in Europe is benefiting from semis volatility with forgiving reactions to mixed results, while US investors are less sympathetic.
Macau October GGR fell 10%, in line with expectations. Jefferies sees the data as neutral and views GEC and WYNN earnings as more likely stock movers.

Asia earnings: Panasonic had record 2Q adjusted OP up over 100% YoY with a raised guide on AI infrastructure demand, Sungrow missed 3Q with ESS GPM of 21% vs 36% in 2Q, and Lingyi iTech was upgraded to Buy after a 20% NP beat.

NSE: 15% revenue and 16% EPS CAGR through FY29 and a justified premium to BSE.

sector_views.rationale: PPC initiated at Buy as the highest growth name in coverage at a sector-average valuation.
Sell-off continues and multiples have compressed, but valuation dispersion and catalysts are creating selective opportunities.
Europe's reaction to mixed results is forgiving, but US investors are less sympathetic, and semis hold the key short term. Jefferies is defensive near term.
More bullish on rent growth after 3Q earnings, with demand from e-commerce, advanced manufacturing and data centers and constrained supply. Expects ~3% annual rent growth 2027-29.
All five covered names screen as relative-value longs vs the S&P 500 and FTSE 100.
Production is declining 3.1% y/y, a structural supply challenge keeping price risk skewed to the upside.
October GGR -10% was in line. Jefferies favors other areas of coverage vs Macau, but GEC and WYNN remain top picks.
Strong Q3 earnings and a broadening earnings thesis. Jefferies remains positive on the S&P 500.

earnings_insights: Rheinmetall Q3 due 5 Nov: Jefferies estimates 39% sales growth and 51% adj. EBIT growth (forecast, not reported).
Leonardo Q3 due 5 Nov: Jefferies estimates 14% sales growth and 29% EBITA growth (forecast), likely supporting a guide upgrade.
Fresenius 3Q results are due Nov 4.
Cameco Q3 reported: EPS C$0.01 (reported) was C$0.35 below Jefferies' estimate and C$0.32 below consensus. Revenue C$619m (+1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA C$267m (-14%), Westinghouse EBITDA +15% to C$143m.
Elm Company reported a 26% clean EPS beat with margins more than 500bp stronger.
Spie Q3 reported: organic growth +4.7%.
Forvia 3Q sales reported slightly ahead, 2026 guidance confirmed.
General Dynamics reported Q3 sales and profit 6% ahead of Jefferies. 2026 EPS estimate raised to $17.35 vs company guide of $17.20-17.30.
Honeywell Aerospace Q3 reported sales 2% ahead and EBIT 7% ahead of Jefferies, with 4pts of tariff help. 2027 EPS estimate cut 4% to $8.65.
Textron: 2026 EPS estimate raised 14% to $6.65 and 2027 to $6.75. Systems growth hit 16%.
Arxis raised 2026 organic growth to +21-22% and printed Q3 margins above 45%.
US 3Q bank recap: 26 of 34 banks beat EPS. PPNR beat at 17 banks, NII at 14 and NIM at 17 vs Jefferies forecasts, and deposits missed at 20 banks.
S&P 500 Q3 (60% reported): earnings growth ~32% and sales growth ~13.5%, EPS beats outperforming by 1.2% on day one and ~3% over one week.
Parsons funded backlog +7% to $6.8B, covering 105% of 2027 revenue estimate.
JinkoSolar 3Q26 reported narrower net loss with GM at 12.3% and ESS shipments at 1.75GWh. 4Q module guidance is 16-18GW.
Sungrow 3Q26 reported a miss: ESS GPM 21% (vs 36% in 2Q) and an RMB500m investment loss.
Westpac FY26 cash earnings reported down 1% YoY to A$6,888m, 1% below Jefferies' estimate and 2% below VA's estimate.
Sumitomo Pharma reported 2Q sales and Core OP beating consensus by 3% and 40%. FY sales and Core OP guidance raised 5% and 15%, with a ¥15 dividend reinstated.
Panasonic 2Q adjusted OP reported up over 100% YoY and +14% QoQ, with a substantial FY guidance raise.
Indian Oil Sep-26 EBITDA of Rs303bn reported, sharply ahead of Jefferies' estimate on refining and inventory gains.
NTPC Sept quarter profit reported 16% above Jefferies' estimate. FY27E renewable addition guidance cut to 5GW from 7-8GW.
Bupa Arabia 3Q26 profit reported 4% above Jefferies' estimate. GWP +16% YoY, net income -5% YoY.
China Merchants Bank 3Q26 revenue growth reported at 6.4%.
Sumitomo Corp Q2 reported net profit ¥157.8bn vs ¥190.1bn in Q1. FY3/27 guidance raised ¥40bn to ¥670bn.
Yamato Kogyo Jul-Sep recurring profit reported +8% to ¥23.9bn. FY recurring profit guidance raised 10% to ¥95.5bn.
Mindray 3Q26 revenue reported +3% YoY, +6% ex-FX.
Shanghai United Imaging 3Q26 overseas revenue reported +50% YoY, 28.3% of sales.
FICO F4Q26 preview: estimates cut significantly to set an F2027 baseline given FHFA rule uncertainty (forecast).
Travel 3Q26 previews: Jefferies is constructive on ABNB, sees EXPE 4Q setup risk on tougher comps, and is cautious on BKNG.
Upcoming earnings: GEC and WYNN (Macau) are seen as likely stock movers with conservatively set estimates. OCBC 3Q26 is due 6 Nov.

Fugro cites costs related to the Middle East war.
